sentences.text: The appellant has filed this Misc. appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 07.08.2018 passed in Claim Case No.21/2018 by the VII Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ujjain (M.P.) challenging the inadequacy of compensation.
2. The brief facts giving rise to this case are that on 27.03.2016 at around 11.30 PM, the appellant had gone out for a walk.
When he reached near Bagheswari Temple, respondent No.1 riding his motorcycle bearing registration number MP-41-MU-0570 in a rash and negligent manner, hit the appellant.
As a result, the appellant sustained grievous head injuries and lost consciousness at the stop.
Passerby took him to the Civil Hospital, Ujjain.
Due to the seriousness of his condition, he was referred to C.H.L. Hospital and later to Medanta Hospital, Indore.
The appellant remained in coma for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17365 2 MA-5898-2018 some time and underwent surgery.
After discharge, he remained under prolonged treatment at his residence at Ujjain.
The accident caused severe loss of memory and comprehension and the appellant now requires constant assistance.
He incurred medical expenses amounting to approximately Rs.8,00,000/- and remained under treatment from 28.03.2016 to 11.04.2016.
2.1 The appellant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act before the Claims Tribunal thereby claimi compensation for above mentioned injuries.

Upon consideration of the material on record, the Claims Tribunal awarded Rs.3,55,000/- for medical expenses,
Rs.25,000/- for physical and mental pain, special diet and attendant and Rs.34,910/- for loss of income of two months, thus, awarding a total compensation of Rs.4,14,910/-.

1 3.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that a meager amount of Rs.25,000/- was awarded for the injuries sustained by him.
He further submits that it is undisputable that the appellant sustained grievous injuries, which have resulted in permanent disability.
He submits that the appellant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 45% and therefore, the Claims Tribunal should have awarded compensation for this permanent disability.
Additionally, he submits that while a lump sum amount of Rs.25,000/- has been awarded for the appellant's pain and suffering, no amount has been provided for the future prospects of the appellant.
Accordingly, he prays for the enhancement of compensation.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that this was a case of simple injury with no permanent damage to the appellant.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17365 3 MA-5898-2018
He further submits that the conclusion of the Claims Tribunal is impeccable and nothing further is to be awarded for permanent disability.
He also supports the conclusion of Tribunal regarding the appellant's comprehension of the situation.
Thus, he supports the findings of the award.

5. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
6.

The discussions made by the Claims Tribunal in para 14 regarding the injury sustained by the appellant on his head and the reference made in para 20 about the nature of that injury in view of the statement of Dr. Abhay Paliwal (AW-2) clearly indicate that the appellant has sustained permanent disability.

7. On perusal of the statement of Dr. Abhay Paliwal (AW-2) and permanent disability certificate (Ex.P-19), it can be seen that the appellant was subjected to a test under the prescription of Indian Disability Evaluation and Assessment Scale (IDEAS).
He scored 9 marks out of a total of 20, which suggests that he has a mental incapacity of 45%, which appears to be permanent in nature.
From these documents and the discussions surrounding them by the Tribunal, it is clear that the appellant has suffered permanent disability,

In the considered view of this Court, the overall permanent disability of the appellant should be taken at 20%.
8.
The Tribunal in para 26 of the award assessed the income of the appellant.
However, there was no elaborate discussion on the same and the income tax returns were considered without addressing the income of the appellant at the time of accident.

In the absence of any statement regarding NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17365 4 MA-5898-2018 the same, the income of the appellant at the time of accident is taken on a notional basis in accordance with the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority at Rs.6,575/- per month for an unskilled labourer.
An addition of 10% is to be made for future prospects considering the age of 53 years at the time of his accident.
9. As such, after the above modifications and additions, the compensation for the appellant's permanent disability would come to Rs.1,90,938/-.
The learned Claims Tribunal has not awarded anything for the loss of amenities, thus, an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded for the same.

10. The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of application before the Claims Tribunal.
11. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands partly allowed.
